correctness.rationale: The photon-coincidence output vector is derived from the physical one-photon-per-mode input and has norm-squared probability; det U proves some path monomial is nonzero. Independent photon vectors yield independent permutation tensors. In the rank N−1 case, a basis-dependent expansion by unique repeated labels gives exact cancellation equations a_(sigma(i N)) = -a_sigma. If two distinct coefficients in the dependence are nonzero, a nonzero monomial forces six nonzero 3-by-3 submatrix monomials to alternate, inconsistent with three row-pair ratio equations. A proportional pair admits explicit balanced-HOM cancellation. In the full-support case, the Gram kernel is precisely the alternating line; its spectral quotient yields the claimed inequality using a unitary determinant projection and the published permanent minimum N!/N^N. The factorial strictness holds for every N≥3 by (k-1)(N-k)≥0 with interior strictness. Explicit finite-dimensional tensor-vs-Gram tests, HOM boundary checks and one quotient-eigenvalue check pass from the supplied standalone script; these diagnostics do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2014 motivating primary source proves only the three-photon linearly dependent nonzero case and conjectures a far broader zero-output statement. The new claim is a finite-rank codimension-one all-dimensions theorem, with an all-unitary positive spectral-gap lower bound for full-support relations. Its proof is neither stated nor implied by the source conjecture or the general counting identity. Inspected later counting formulas and special Sylvester-network suppression laws do not assert or imply the all-unitary rank N−1 classification. Exact priority remains uncertain beyond available indexed literature and a related broad review accessible only at abstract level.
residual_risks: An equivalent result could appear as an unindexed specialization of representation theory or linear-optical distinguishability literature.
The broad multiparticle-interference review arXiv:1410.7687 was only accessible at abstract level; it was not characterized as definitively not covering the claim.
The quantitative lower bound need not be sharp and depends on the chosen internal-state Gram matrix.

value.rationale: Exact vanishing of all-port coincidence is a physically motivated sharp interference test, and internal rank N−1 is the first singular stratum next to full distinguishability. The theorem gives a natural complete all-N classification of possible perfect suppression within that stratum, extends the 2014 three-photon established case, and yields a strictly positive robust all-unitary quantitative certificate for full-support relations. The precise spectral-quotient bound is mathematically motivated by the alternating representation and has direct use for excluding exact zero coincidence without optimizing network design; it is not a free renaming or an arbitrary small numerical gain.
